**3B.8 Research Note: Ali Khamenei (2024)**

**Bottom line:** I found no convincing evidence that Khamenei allowed peaceful protest, dissent, or community organization without retaliation or chilling surveillance in 2024. The record is dominated by surveillance, arrests, torture, execution, and selective punishment. The only counter-signal I found is discretionary clemency for some inmates, which is too narrow to count as genuine protection of protest rights.

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| [Iran: Draconian campaign to enforce compulsory veiling laws through surveillance and mass car confiscations](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/03/iran-draconian-campaign-to-enforce-compulsory-veiling-laws-through-surveillance-and-mass-car-confiscations/) | Amnesty International | 2024-03-06 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/03/iran-draconian-campaign-to-enforce-compulsory-veiling-laws-through-surveillance-and-mass-car-confiscations/ | Amnesty documented widespread surveillance, police checks, confiscations, prosecutions, flogging, and “morality” classes used to police behavior. This is strong evidence of chilling surveillance and coercive social control, not tolerance for organizing or dissent. | 3B.8; also 3B.5, 3B.2 |
| [Iran security forces rape, torture detainees](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/04/22/iran-security-forces-rape-torture-detainees) | Human Rights Watch | 2024-04-22 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/04/22/iran-security-forces-rape-torture-detainees | HRW documented rape, torture, sexual assault, and coerced false confessions during the crackdown on protests. This is direct evidence that dissent triggered violent retaliation rather than safe public protest space. | 3B.8; also 3B.1, 3B.2, 3B.4 |
| [Iran: No effective investigations into security-force abuses](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/iran-two-years-after-woman-life-freedom-uprising-impunity-for-crimes-reigns-supreme/) | Amnesty International | 2024-09-11 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/iran-two-years-after-woman-life-freedom-uprising-impunity-for-crimes-reigns-supreme/ | Amnesty said authorities still had not carried out impartial investigations into killings, torture, sexual violence, or disappearances, and instead harassed victims’ families with arbitrary detention. That supports a climate of retaliation and intimidation around dissent. | 3B.8; also 3B.1, 3B.2, 3B.4, 3B.6 |
| [Iran chokehold on dissent](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/iran-chokehold-dissent) | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-11 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/iran-chokehold-dissent | HRW reported authorities killed hundreds of protesters, arrested thousands, tortured detainees, and failed to open transparent investigations into security-force abuse. This is strong evidence against permitting peaceful protest or independent civic organization. | 3B.8; also 3B.1, 3B.2, 3B.4 |
| [Leader approves pardoning, commuting sentences of about 3,000 Iranian convicts](https://www.presstv.ir/Detail/2024/09/20/733636/Leader-approves-pardoning-convicts) | Press TV | 2024-09-20 | https://www.presstv.ir/Detail/2024/09/20/733636/Leader-approves-pardoning-convicts | Khamenei approved pardons or commutations for 2,887 convicts, including some security-related cases and minors. This is the clearest limited positive signal, but it is discretionary clemency, not a demonstrated right to protest or organize. | 3B.8; also 3B.1 |
| [Iran executes 853 people in eight-year high amid relentless repression and renewed war on drugs](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/04/iran-executes-853-people-in-eight-year-high-amid-relentless-repression-and-renewed-war-on-drugs/) | Amnesty International | 2024-04-04 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/04/iran-executes-853-people-in-eight-year-high-amid-relentless-repression-and-renewed-war-on-drugs/ | Amnesty reported a major execution surge, including mass use of the death penalty after unfair Revolutionary Court trials. This reinforces that the state response to dissent and insecurity was punitive rather than permissive. | 3B.8; also 3B.1, 3B.2 |

**Search gap**
- I found no reliable 2024 evidence that Khamenei permitted peaceful protest or community organization without retaliation.
- I also found no credible evidence of reduced surveillance or fewer arbitrary restrictions on dissent.
- The only positive material was limited clemency, which does not amount to a broader tolerance of protest rights.
